description:
I'm a Computer Science Engineering student passionate about space exploration, simulation technology, and AI-powered applications. I'm currently developing Sol Mission Simulator, an interactive space mission simulator designed to let users plan missions, make spacecraft engineering decisions, manage resources, and explore the consequences of their choices.

I want to build more than a visually impressive simulation—I want to create an engaging educational game that makes complex space engineering concepts easier to understand through hands-on experimentation.

I'm looking for motivated teammates who are excited about space, science, and problem-solving. In particular, I'd love to collaborate with people who have skills or interests in:
• Web development and JavaScript/TypeScript
• Three.js, 3D graphics, and interactive simulations
• Astronomy, orbital mechanics, aerospace engineering, or physics
• Game design, UI/UX, and visual storytelling
• AI, scientific research, testing, and technical writing

You don't need to be an expert in everything. Curiosity, teamwork, creativity, and a willingness to learn are just as important. If you'd like to help turn an ambitious space mission game into a functional, engaging, and educational experience, I'd be happy to connect!
summary: VORQASTRA is an interactive, browser-based space mission design game and 3D astrodynamics simulator built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Players step into the shoes of NASA mission planners, balancing mass, electrical power, communications, and a $1,200M budget across authentic NASA Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–6). Featuring 29 Keplerian celestial bodies, real launch vehicles, four specialist roles, and manual 6-DOF spacecraft flight, VORQASTRA transforms complex aerospace systems engineering into an engaging, accessible learning experience.
details:
VORQASTRA's Project Solution

Space exploration is humanity's pinnacle of multidisciplinary systems engineering. When NASA conceives a planetary exploration mission—whether landing humans at the lunar South Pole under Artemis, surveying Europa with Europa Clipper, searching for past life with Perseverance, or returning pristine samples from asteroid 101955 Bennu—mission planners must balance tightly coupled technical, financial, and environmental constraints. Traditional educational tools either oversimplify space into passive 3D planetarium models devoid of engineering consequences, or present dry, complex desktop software that alienates students. VORQASTRA bridges this gap as a zero-plugin WebGL mission formulation simulator that transforms abstract aerospace equations into an engaging, consequence-driven game.

Minimalist, high-contrast VORQASTRA landing interface introducing learners to interactive planetary exploration.

How Does Our Solution Work? VORQASTRA merges real Keplerian astrodynamics across 29 celestial bodies (with time acceleration up to 1,000,000x) with authentic NASA phase-gate systems engineering:

  • Mission Design Wizard & Rocket Scaling: Players configure target destinations (Moon, Mars, Bennu, Outer Planets), mission architectures (Orbiter, Lander, Probe, Sample Return), and scientific objectives. Launch vehicles enforce realistic destination payload derating (LEO 100%, Moon 32%, Mars 25%, Bennu 24%, Outer Planets 14%, Sun 6%), triggering immediate visual alerts if a spacecraft exceeds launch capacity.

Mission Design Wizard configuring target worlds, mission architectures, and science objectives.

  • The 6-Resource Consequence Engine & Specialist Roles: A reactive engineering dashboard dynamically links Spacecraft Wet Mass, Electrical Power Balance, Fiscal Budget ($1,200M cap), Daily Data Volume, Deep Space Downlink Bitrate, and Mission Lifetime. Selecting high-power instruments demands larger solar/nuclear power systems and heavier rockets, directly impacting costs and Deep Space Network (DSN) signal margins. Players toggle between four operational lenses: Mission Commander, Spacecraft Systems Engineer, Science Specialist, and Operations Specialist.

Reactive 6-Resource Engineering Dashboard and Spacecraft Systems Engineer interface tracking live mass, power, budget, and DSN margins.

  • Planetary Inspector & Arrival Intelligence: Deep physical and orbital telemetry panels display real-time planetary radius, mass, surface gravity, atmospheric pressure, and dynamic distance in Astronomical Units (AU), paired with automated arrival reports evaluating human survivability metrics (surface temperature, pressure, and cosmic radiation hazards).

Planetary Inspector displaying real-time physical constants, orbital telemetry, and live distance metrics for Mars.

  • Canted Propulsion Geometry & 6-DOF Free Exploration: Free Exploration Mode offers uncapped manual spacecraft piloting with authentic Space Shuttle Main Engine (SSME) nozzles canted 17.6° upward and 10° toe-out, quaternion thrust alignment, additive particle smoke trails, and a 360° internal avionics cockpit.Canted Space Shuttle Main Engine (SSME) nozzles firing luminous flame cones, radial glow sprites, and particle smoke trails.
  • NASA Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–6): An interactive progression modal guides learners through formal NASA project formulation phase gates—from initial science goals to flight readiness review—presenting ten structured educational criteria per stage.

Interactive NASA Concept Maturity Level (CML 1–6) modal teaching formal aerospace phase-gate systems engineering.

The Simulator Benefits & Our Goal

  • Demystifies Systems Engineering: Teaches students why space missions take years to design and how engineering trade-offs govern mission viability.
  • Connects Physics to Practice: Turns textbook aerospace formulas (Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, vis-viva orbital velocity, inverse-square solar irradiance, and free-space path loss) into immediate visual feedback.
  • Accessible STEM Education: Runs smoothly in any modern browser over Cloudflare Pages Edge CDN with zero downloads or hardware barriers.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • 3D Rendering & Motion: Three.js (WebGL) and GreenSock (GSAP) for cinematic camera easing and coordinate transformations.
  • Procedural Graphics & Physics: Custom Simplex Noise canvas shaders (earthTex) for Earth landmasses/bathymetry/clouds, Keplerian orbital propagators, and quaternion propulsion vector math.
  • Audio Pipeline: Multi-bus Web Audio API graph (AudioManager) featuring dynamic compression and filtered 360° cockpit cabin acoustics.
  • Deployment & Version Control: Cloudflare Pages Edge CDN ([https://vorqastra.pages.dev/](https://vorqastra.pages.dev/)) and GitHub ([https://github.com/bhawsarhardik195-blip/VORQASTRA](https://github.com/bhawsarhardik195-blip/VORQASTRA)).
